51580545.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to TLR2 (unknown origin) assessed as dissociation constant by SPR analysis

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods - Surface plasmon: Biacore T100 was used to measure binding affinities. The active TLR2 protein was diluted in sodium acetate solution (pH 4.5) to a concentration of 20 μg/mL and then immobilized on a -COOH sensor chip by amine coupling to reach target densities of 9100 resonance units (RU). The running buffer was PBS containing 5 % DMSO. Data were recorded at 25 °C. Then, different concentrations of 5 were injected at a flow rate of 30 μL/min with a contact time of 60 s and a dissociation time of 60 s. Sensorgrams were analysed using BiacoreT100 Analysis Software. The KD affinity constant values were calculated by kinetic analysis or the steady-state affinity method.
original_paragraph.Figure 12 caption: Fig. 12. The binding affinity of 5 to TLR2 was analysed using SPR.
original_paragraph.Results - 3.2. Surface plasmon resonance: The SPR assay was used to further confirm the interaction between the TLR2 protein and 5. As shown in Fig. 12, 5 exhibited concentration-dependent binding to the TLR2 protein. The KD value of the dissociation constant for 5 was 3.56 μM, indicating that 5 stably binds with TLR2, which is probably a target of 5.
original_paragraph.Figure 12 sensorgram data: The sensorgram in Fig. 12 shows response (RU) over time (s). The concentrations of compound 5 are labeled on the plot: 3 μM (green), 6.25 μM (yellow), 12.5 μM (blue), 25 μM (orange), and 100 μM (purple). The association phase lasts for 60 s (from 0 to 60 s), followed by a 60 s dissociation phase (from 60 to 120 s). The KD value is explicitly stated as 3.56 μM in the text.
